evidence.reason: The no-tag path is documented at lines 783-788 as deliberately ancestry-only: "A merged main SHA is deployable on its own: the ancestry check below is the whole rule, and the deploy path names no tag," with the caller supplying a resolved merged-main SHA. An annotated tag object ID peels to that same commit for merge-base, ls-tree, show and checkout, so accepting it does not admit an undeployable revision or change what is deployed; it only means the regex at 790 does not enforce object type, which the docstring and the recent guard-dropping history treat as out of scope. The asserted record/switch-return mismatch is not shown in the supplied code and, even if present, would be a pre-existing accepted consequence rather than a correctness defect in deployment. Requiring cat-file -t commit therefore adds validation scope beyond the documented rule rather than repairing an implementation error.
